title: The Boy and the King: The Martyrs of the Trench
overview: This episode recounts the spread of Christianity in Yemen through the miraculous story of a young boy who chose faith over sorcery. It details the brutal martyrdom of twenty thousand believers in the 'trench of fire' and the subsequent conquest of Yemen by the Abyssinian army led by Abrahah.
lessons: Sincerity in seeking truth leads to divine guidance, as seen in the boy's transition from magic to tawhid.
True success is measured by guidance and the afterlife, not by physical survival in this world.
One person's sacrifice can be the catalyst for the guidance of an entire nation.
Allah is the ultimate controller of life and death; no harm can reach a person except by His permission.
The story of the talking baby demonstrates that Allah provides support and 'thabat' (steadfastness) to believers during their most difficult trials.

chapters.title: Christianity's Entry into Najran
chapters.summary: The lecture begins with the story of Faymiyun, a pious Christian monk from Sham who was kidnapped and sold into slavery in Najran. His master witnessed Faymiyun's devotion and the miracles granted to him by Allah, leading to a challenge against the city's idol-worshipping traditions. Faymiyun prayed for the destruction of a sacred tree worshipped by the people, and when a lightning bolt destroyed it, the population of Najran accepted Christianity. This event established the religion of tawhid in the region before the arrival of Islam.
key_points: Faymiyun was a monk from Sham (Greater Syria) who practiced the true tawhid of Isa alayhis-salam.
Najran is a city bordering Yemen that became a center for Christianity.
A lightning bolt miracle destroyed the worshipped tree, leading to mass conversion.
The religion was the true, uncorrupted Christianity based on the Injil.

chapters.title: The Boy, the Monk, and the Sorcerer
chapters.summary: During the reign of the tyrannical King Dhu Nuwas in Yemen, a young boy was selected to learn magic from the king's aging sorcerer. On his daily journey to the mountain to learn witchcraft, the boy encountered a Christian monk and became mesmerized by his recitation of the Injil. For a time, the boy balanced both educations, learning magic by day and the religion of Isa alayhis-salam in secret. The monk advised the boy on how to handle the magician's punishments for his lateness, keeping their meetings hidden from the king.
key_points: Dhu Nuwas was the son of Tibban As'ad but became a corrupt and tyrannical ruler.
The king employed magicians to maintain power and control over the people.
The intelligent boy was chosen to inherit the chief magician's legacy.
The boy learned the Injil secretly from a monk living on the path to the mountain.

chapters.title: Miracles and the Proof of Truth
chapters.summary: The boy sought a sign from Allah to determine whether the monk's path or the magician's path was superior. He used a stone to kill a terrifying beast blocking the road, praying that if the monk was more beloved to Allah, the creature would die. After the beast was slain, the monk informed the boy that he had surpassed him and warned of upcoming trials. The boy was granted the power to heal the blind and lepers through du'a, eventually curing a blind official in Dhu Nuwas's court who then accepted tawhid.
key_points: The boy killed a great beast with a stone as a test of faith.
The monk prophesied that the boy would face significant tests (fitnah).
Allah granted the boy miracles of healing blindness and leprosy.
A royal court official converted to faith after being cured of blindness.

chapters.title: The Failed Executions
chapters.summary: King Dhu Nuwas discovered the boy's faith after torturing the cured official and the monk, both of whom were eventually executed by being sawed in half. The king then attempted to execute the boy by throwing him off a mountain and drowning him in the sea. However, each time the king's men attempted the execution, Allah intervened with earthquakes and storms, killing the guards while the boy returned to the palace unharmed. These events served as a demonstration that Allah is the sole Giver of Life and Giver of Death.
key_points: The monk and the blind official were martyred by being sawed in two.
Allah saved the boy from being thrown off a mountain via an earthquake.
The king's men drowned in the sea while the boy was miraculously spared.
The events emphasized Allah's names: al-Muhyi (The Giver of Life) and al-Mumit (The Giver of Death).

chapters.title: The Supreme Sacrifice of the Ghulam
chapters.summary: Recognizing that the king could not kill him through ordinary means, the boy offered a specific method for his own execution to guide the people. He instructed Dhu Nuwas to gather all the people and shoot him with an arrow while proclaiming, 'In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy.' The king followed the instructions, and the boy died, but the crowd immediately realized the king's lack of power and the truth of the boy's God. This resulted in the entire population of the city declaring their faith in Christianity and the Lord of the Ghulam.
key_points: The boy provided the king with the only method to kill him.
The phrase 'Bismillahi Rabbil-Ghulam' was required for the execution to succeed.
The boy sacrificed his life in this dunya for the eternal guidance of his people.
The entire city converted to the religion of tawhid after witnessing the execution.

chapters.title: The People of the Trench
chapters.summary: Infuriated by the mass conversion, Dhu Nuwas ordered deep trenches to be dug and filled with fire, demanding that the believers either renounce their faith or be burned alive. Approximately twenty thousand people chose martyrdom in the fires, showing incredible steadfastness. A famous miracle occurred during this massacre when a nursing baby spoke to his hesitant mother, encouraging her to stay firm on the truth. These events are immortalized in the Qur'an in Surah al-Buruj, which curses the 'People of the Trench' for their cruelty against believers.
key_points: Dhu Nuwas killed 20,000 believers in one day using trenches of fire.
A nursing baby spoke by Allah's permission to strengthen his mother's iman.
Ashab al-Ukhdud (The People of the Trench) are mentioned in Surah al-Buruj.
The believers were persecuted solely for their belief in Allah al-Aziz al-Hamid.

chapters.title: The Abyssinian Conquest of Yemen
chapters.summary: A single survivor of the trench massacre, Daws Dhu Tha'laban, escaped on horseback and sought help from the Emperor of Sham, who then petitioned the Najashi of Abyssinia. The Najashi, a Christian king, sent an army to Yemen to avenge the slaughtered believers. This army was led by the generals Aryat and Abrahah, who successfully defeated Dhu Nuwas and took control of Yemen. This conquest ended the Himyarite dynasty and established Abyssinian rule, setting the stage for the Year of the Elephant and the birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
key_points: Daws Dhu Tha'laban was the sole survivor who carried the news to the Emperor of Sham.
The Najashi of Abyssinia (Ethiopia) sent a retaliatory army of Christians.
Aryat and Abrahah were the two primary leaders of the Abyssinian forces.
Dhu Nuwas died by drowning while attempting to flee the invasion.
The Abyssinians ruled Yemen for roughly 70 years following this conquest.

segments.translit: Bismillāhir-Raḥmānir-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbil-'ālamīn. Wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka 'alā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa 'alā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajma'īn. Rabbi-shraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī wa-ḥlul 'uqdatan min lisānī yafqahū qawlī. Allāhumma 'allimnā mā yanfa'unā wanfa'nā bimā 'allamtanā wa zidnā 'ilmā.

segments.text: Insha'Allah today we will start where we left off last week.
Last week we spoke about how Christianity entered [[Najran|نجران]].
And [[Najran|نجران]] is a city in present day Saudi Arabia that borders [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And we spoke about [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]], [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] who was a Christian monk from [[Sham|شام]], from Greater Syria.

And he went to Africa to do [[dawah|دَعْوَة]], to call people to the [[din|دِين]] of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], the true religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], the religion of [[tawhid|توحيد]].

So he went to Africa to call the people to [[tawhid|توحيد]], and while he was in Africa, a gang kidnapped him, and they sold him into slavery. And the person who bought him was a man from [[Najran|نجران]].
So this man bought him and took him back to [[Najran|نجران]] where [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] served as his slave.
And this man saw [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] practicing his religion, the religion of Christianity, the religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], the religion of [[tawhid|توحيد]].
And he saw some of the miracles that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] had granted to this man, and he was amazed at it.
And he got into a conversation with him.
And [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] wanted his master to accept Christianity, to accept [[tawhid|توحيد]], but he was hesitant to do so.
And at that time, the people of [[Najran|نجران]], they had a tree that they used to worship.
So [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] said to his master, 'If my Lord, or if my God, destroys your god, then will you believe in my God?'
And he said, 'Of course, if your God destroys my god, then I will believe in your God.' So he said, 'Okay, gather the people...'
...in front of that tree that you worship, and let us see who is victorious.' So he said okay, he gathered the people of [[Najran|نجران]] to witness.

And [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] started making [[du'a|دُعَاء]] to Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] to show these people a sign, to destroy this tree, this object of their worship, this false god of theirs.
[[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] made [[du'a|دُعَاء]] to Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] to destroy that tree, and Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] answered his [[du'a|دُعَاء]]...
...and sent a bolt of lightning that destroyed that tree. And when the people witnessed this...
...they believed in Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], they accepted the religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], and they became Christians.
So this is how Christianity entered [[Najran|نجران]].
Now, a group of those Christians...
...led by a man named Abdullah ibn Thamir, a group of them went from [[Najran|نجران]] to [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And we know at that time, as we spoke about last week, the ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]] at that time was [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]].
And [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] was a man who was corrupted in his beliefs.
Even though his father, [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], who we spoke about previously, his father accepted Judaism...
...and he was the first man who covered the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] with [[Kiswah|كسوة]]. He was a good man.
But this son of his, [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], he became corrupted.
And he had a lot of magicians that he used to employ in his court...
...and he used them to hold on to his power and his control over the people.
So these Christians who went from [[Najran|نجران]] to [[Yemen|اليمن]]...
...they practiced their religion secretly. They didn't expose themselves as Christians because they knew if [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]]...
...were to find out about their affair, that they were Christians and they were on the religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], that he would harm them or he would perhaps kill them.
So [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]]...
...he, as we said, he employed many magicians, and his chief magician...
...his most powerful magician was getting very old.
So he told [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], this magician, he told [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], he said, 'I'm getting old...
...and you know, I don't know how much time I have left. I want to teach this witchcraft, I want to teach magic to someone so they can carry on my legacy after I pass away.'

So [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] understood this, and he thought that that would be something for his benefit as well. He thought, 'Okay, if my chief magician dies, I need someone who knows magic like he does so I can hold on to my kingdom and keep control the way I want to keep control.'
So he agreed to this request from his chief magician...
...and he found a young boy who was very intelligent, who was very smart.
So [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] selected this boy...
...to learn magic from this chief magician.
And this chief magician, he used to live on a mountain top.
So [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], the king, he sent this young boy to go learn magic from this magician. So every day...
...the young boy, he would walk from his home to the...
...dwelling of the magician, which was on top of the mountain. So he would make this journey every day: going to the magician, learning magic, and then coming back to his home.
Now, on the way from the boy's home to the magician's home on the mountain...
...on the way, there was a dwelling of a monk, a Christian monk, one of those Christians who had come from [[Najran|نجران]]...
...who had settled in [[Yemen|اليمن]]. So his house happened to be on the way from the boy's house to the magician's house.
So when the boy would walk to the magician's house to learn magic, on the way, he would pass by this Christian monk's house, and he would hear him...
...reciting the Injil.
He would hear him reciting the Injil, and he became mesmerized by this, and he was very impressed with it. So...
...on his way to the magician, he started stopping by the monk's house for some time and speaking to him...
...and learning about Christianity from him.
And then when he spent some time with the monk, he would continue on his journey to...
...the magician's house on the mountain, and he would learn magic from the magician. So he was learning Christianity from the monk and magic from the magician at the same time.
Now of course...
...he would spend some time with the monk learning the Injil, and then when he would go to the magician's house, he would be late.
He would not be there on time because he was spending too much time with the monk.
So the magician would berate him. The magician would punish him whenever he came late.
So he told the monk that this is what's happening. 'Now every day I'm coming to the magician's house and I'm late every day because I'm stopping on the way to speak with you...'
...'and whenever he sees that I come late, he punishes me.' So the monk said to the boy...
...he said, 'If you go late to the magician's house, just tell him that your family caused you to be late.
And if you are late going back to your family's house, then tell them that the magician kept you late.
So that they don't punish you, and they don't say anything to you...
...and they don't find out about us. They don't find out about you and me speaking to each other.
Just blame your lateness at the magician's house on your family, and blame your lateness back to your family on the magician.
And don't say anything about me. You don't want the people to find out that you are coming and speaking to me and learning from me.'
So this continued for some time.
The young boy, he would go and speak to the Christian monk and learn Christianity from him, and then he would go to the magician and learn magic from him.
One day when he was on his way, on the road there was this big type of creature, a big creature...
...and the people were unable to pass...
...go past that creature. They were scared of it.
So the young boy saw this as an opportunity to see...
...who is actually teaching me the right thing. Should I follow the religion of this Christian monk, or should I continue...
...with the magician?
So he said, 'This beast in the middle of the road, this is a perfect opportunity for me to find out...
...what the right path is.' So he picked up a stone...
...and he said...
'O Allah, if the...
...Christian monk is more beloved to You than the sorcerer, if the Christian monk is more beloved to You than this magician...
...then kill this beast, kill this creature.' And he threw the stone at the creature...
...and the creature died.

The creature died. So this was his proof. This was the proof that the boy asked for, and from that point on, he knew that the religion of [[tawhid|توحيد]], the religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] alone is worthy of worship...
This is the true path.
So he went to the monk, and he told him about what happened.
And then the monk told him, "Today, you have become better than me.
Today, you are greater than me. But I fear that some trial will come to you now.
I fear that some test is going to come to you now. So be aware that you may be tested."

And this young boy, he became so close to Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], so devoted to Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] gave him many miracles.
Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] gave this young boy many miracles. Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] would cure blind people through him.
Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] would cure people who had the disease of leprosy through this boy, and other diseases as well.
This boy would make [[du'a|دُعَاء]] to Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] to cure these people, and Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] would cure them.

And this became known. The people started talking about it, and the people came to know that this boy, people who go to him, he asks Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] for these needs, and Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] answers his [[du'a|دُعَاء]].
So there was one man who worked for [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]]. He was in the royal court of [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], and he was blind.
And when he came to know about this boy, he thought that, "I can go to this boy, and I can see again."
So this man who worked in the court of the king, [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], he went to the boy and he said that, "I hear that you cure people from blindness. I hear that you cure people from blindness."
And the boy said, "No, I do not cure anyone. Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is the one who cures."

And then he said, "Okay, what do I need to do to be cured of my blindness?" He said, "You need to believe in Allah. Believe that it is Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] alone worthy of worship without any partner. Believe in Allah."

He said, "Okay, I believe in Allah." Then the boy made [[du'a|دُعَاء]] to Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] to cure this man of his blindness. And Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] cured him, and the man could see again.
Now, as we said, this man, he worked in the royal court, he was always with the king.
So one day he sat in his normal place in the court of the king, and the king saw that his blindness was cured.
So he asked him, "How did your eyesight come back? How are you able to see?" And the man replied, "Allah cured me. Allah cured me."
So the king was surprised at this. "What are you talking about? What is this new thing that you're bringing up?"
So he started to ask him questions about where did he get this new belief. And this man remained silent. He wouldn't tell the king. He wouldn't tell him anything. He didn't tell him about the boy.
But the king continued to torture him and torture him and torture him until finally he told him about the boy.
So then the king, he knew that this is the same boy that I was sending for magic. So he called for that boy to come in front of him.
And he said to him, "You have learned so much magic now that you are able to cure people of blindness and leprosy?"
And then he said, "No, it's not magic, and it's not me who is curing them. It is Allah. It is Allah alone who is curing them."

So then the king became very angry. He became so angry because this is the boy that he selected to go learn magic from the magician, and instead he learned [[tawhid|توحيد]], and Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is granting him miracles through this belief.
So he became very mad at the boy, and he said to the boy, "Who taught you this? Who taught you this?"
And the boy refused to speak. He wouldn't say anything about the monk that he was learning from.
Until he was tortured and tortured and tortured so much that finally he said, "I learned this from such-and-such Christian monk."

So the king ordered for that Christian monk to be brought in front of him. And he said to him, "Renounce your religion right now. Renounce the religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]. Renounce the religion of [[tawhid|توحيد]]."
And the monk refused. He said, "I will not renounce it." So the king ordered for him to be executed by bringing a saw and cutting him in two pieces through his head. So he was cut into two pieces.

And this was witnessed by the boy and by the man who worked in the court of the king who was cured from his blindness. They both saw this happening. So this is how they killed the monk, the king killed the monk.

Then he took that man who worked in his court, the man who was cured for blindness, and he said the same thing to him. The king said the same thing to him, "Renounce this religion. Renounce your religion."
And the man refused. He said, "I will not renounce it." So he ordered the same thing to be done to him. So he was sawed in half. His body was split into two pieces and he was executed in this manner.

So the boy witnessed both of these executions. He witnessed his teacher, the Christian monk, being executed, and he also witnessed this man of the royal court who was cured of blindness, he also witnessed him being executed.
So the king thought that, "Okay, he's going to see this, and he will learn his lesson, and he will leave this religion."

So he said to the young boy, "Now you renounce your religion, or I'm going to kill you like I killed them." But the boy, he remained firm on his [[iman|إيمان]], and he refused to renounce the religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]. He refused to renounce the religion of [[tawhid|توحيد]].
So the king ordered for his execution. But he didn't order for his execution in the same way. Rather, he gathered some of his court and he said to them,
"Take him on the top of a mountain. Take him on the top of a mountain and throw him down from that mountain. This is how we are going to execute this boy."

So he sent his men with this boy to the top of the mountain. So they're at the top of the mountain, and they're about to throw him down, and then Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] causes a big earthquake to happen.
Right at that moment, a big earthquake happens, and all of those people, the king's men, they fall off the mountain, but the boy is safe, he's okay.

So all of the king's men are dead, and the kid is safe, and he goes back to the king. And the king is surprised to see him. He said, "What happened? What happened to all of the people? I sent them to go and throw you off the mountain. How are you back here? Where are they?"
And then he said that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] saved me from them.

So the king was very angry now. He's very upset. He gathered another group of his men and he said, "Go take him into the deep sea. Take him into the sea and throw him in the sea, drown him in the sea."

So a group of the men, they took a boat, and they took the boy, and they went deep into the sea. Then Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] caused the waves to become very powerful and strong, and Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] caused those people who were in that boat to fall out of the boat, and they fell into the water and they all drowned except the boy. He survived. He survived.

And he came back to the king again. Now the king is very shocked and surprised. Every time he's sending for this boy to be executed, he's coming back safe and sound, and his men are the ones who are dying instead of the boy dying.

So whatever way he tried to kill him, he was unable to kill him. And this shows us a lesson that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is the one who gives life and the one who causes death. Even if the whole world wants to conspire to kill you, but Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] doesn't want you to die, you're not going to die. And even if the whole world conspires to keep you alive, if Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] has written that you're going to die, you're going to die.
Allah is [[al-Muhyi|المحيي]] [[wa al-Mumit|والمميت]]. He is the one who gives life, and He is the one who causes death, and nobody shares this power with Him.
So the king was seeing this. The king was seeing that this boy, no matter how we try to kill him, he's just not dying.

So the boy actually gives the king a suggestion. He says, "You want to kill me? You want to kill me? I will tell you the way, the only way that you can kill me. I will tell you the only way that you can possibly kill me."
So [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] says, "Okay, tell me. What should I do? What do I need to do to finally get rid of you, to kill you?"
So he said, "You need to gather the people. You need to gather all the people. You can't just do this privately. All the people have to witness this. Gather the people,
and tie me up to the trunk of a tree. Gather the people to witness and tie me up to the trunk of a tree. And then take an arrow..."
from my quiver, and just before you're about to shoot me with it, say [[Bismillahi Rabbil-Ghulam|بِسْمِ اللهِ رَبِّ الْغُلَامِ]].
Say [[Bismillahi Rabbil-Ghulam|بِسْمِ اللهِ رَبِّ الْغُلَامِ]].
Just before you're about to shoot the arrow at me, say, 'In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy.'
So the king is desperate. The king really wants to get rid of this boy. So he says, 'Okay, I'll do it.'
So he gathers all of the people. He ties the boy to the tree. The arrow is taken out of the quiver. He says, '[[Bismillahi Rabbil-Ghulam|بِسْمِ اللهِ رَبِّ الْغُلَامِ]].'

Now think about this. Everyone is watching this, and these people who are witnessing this, they know about the attempts on this boy's life. They know that the king tried to kill him by throwing him off a mountain, they know that the king tried to kill him by throwing him into the ocean, they know that the king has tried multiple times to kill this boy, and he wasn't able to do it.

Now when he says, '[[Bismillahi Rabbil-Ghulam|بِسْمِ اللهِ رَبِّ الْغُلَامِ]], in the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy,' and then he shoots the arrow, and it hits the boy in the head, and the boy dies.

The boy dies. But everybody witnessed that the king had no power to kill this boy on his own from the previous attempts, but once he said, 'In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy,' then he was able to kill him.
So that flicked the light on in the minds of the people. They said, 'Look, this king has no power. He has no power to do anything.'
It is Allah alone, the Lord of this boy, who is able to do all things. The only way that he was able to kill that boy was by getting the permission of Allah, the Lord of that boy, to do it.
So once they witnessed this, all of them said, '[[Amanna bi-Rabbil-Alamin|آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ]], [[Amanna bi-Rabbil-Ghulam|آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْغُلَامِ]].'

'We believe in the Lord of the boy. We believe in the Lord of the boy.' And all of them accepted Christianity, they became Christians. They accepted the [[din|دِين]] of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
So [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]]'s plan backfired on him. The reason why he wanted to kill this boy was so that this boy could not spread his religion to the people.
But by killing him, it actually had the opposite effect. The people saw the way that he died, and they all accepted the religion of this boy. So the king's plan backfired on him.
The people plan, and Allah plans, but Allah is the best of planners.
So the people became Christians. They accepted the [[din|دِين]] of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]], and the boy, he sacrificed himself in order for the people to be guided to the truth.

Look at the sacrifice this boy gave. He sacrificed his own life. He is the one who told the king how to kill him. He is the one who gave the king instructions on how to kill him. And the reason why he did this was because he was ready to give his life in the way of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].

He was ready to lose his life in this [[dunya|دُنْيَا]] for the pleasure of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] so that so many people would be guided, and he would get the [[ajr|أَجْر]], he would get the reward for those people being guided to Islam, to the religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]].
So he was willing to sacrifice his life. He sacrificed his life, and the people were guided through him to the correct path. [[SubhanAllah|سُبْحَانَ اللهِ]], beautiful.
So all of them accepted Christianity. The king is very mad now, and he's so upset that he's losing control over his people.
So he orders his army to dig deep trenches, to dig deep trenches along the roads.
And he fills those trenches with fire. He lights a fire and fills those trenches with fire.

And then he gathers the people, all of those people who witnessed what happened with the boy, who became Christians, he said to them, 'Either you renounce your religion, or be thrown into these trenches of fire.'
So they stood firm. They held firm to their religion, and they were thrown in those fires, and they were killed in that way.

So they would go up to the people and say, 'Do you renounce your religion?' And they would say, 'No, we do not renounce our religion. We believe in Allah,' and they would be pushed into the fire. And this kept happening to all of them.
And then the turn came for a woman, a woman who had a young baby with her, a young baby who was still nursing.

And she had [[rahmah|رَحْمَة]], she had some feeling of mercy for that baby. So when it came her turn to be pushed into that trench, and she was asked, 'Do you renounce your religion?', she hesitated a little bit, because she didn't want to go into that fire with her baby. So she hesitated a little bit.
And then Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] caused that baby to speak to his mother. And the baby said to the mother, 'Don't worry, mother. Hold firm. You are on the truth.'
So that gave her a boost of [[iman|إِيمَان]], and she said, 'No, I do not renounce my religion,' and she was thrown into the fire as well.
And it is said that [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] killed 20,000 people in one day by throwing them into these trenches of fire. 20,000 people.

So this was the evil deed that he committed. For these people accepting the truth, [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] killed them and slaughtered them in the most brutal way by burning them alive. And this story is mentioned in [[Suratul-Buruj|سُورَة الْبُرُوج]].
Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] curses those people who threw the believers in the trench that was filled with fire.
And [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] and his army and his men were just sitting and watching these people be killed, and they were witnessing this evil act.
And the only reason that they did this to them, the only reason that they slaughtered them in this way is because they believed in Allah, the Most Mighty, the Praise-Worthy.
So this story is recounted in [[Suratul-Buruj|سُورَة الْبُرُوج]].
So he killed 20,000 of these people in one day. He killed all of them except one. One man was able to escape. One man was able to escape.
And his name was [[Daws Dhu Tha'laban|دَوْس ذُو ثَعْلَبَان]].

He was a Christian who witnessed what happened with the boy, and he accepted Christianity. But they were not able to push him into the trench of fire. He jumped on a horse and he escaped. He jumped on a horse and he escaped. And he's the only one who escaped.
And they tried to follow him, they tried to chase him, but they were unable to chase him.
So he went all the way to the Emperor of [[Sham|شَام]]. He went all the way to the Emperor of [[Sham|شَام]] and told him about what happened.
He told him that [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] did this to the people. He slaughtered the people in this way for believing in Christianity.
So when the Emperor of [[Sham|شَام]] heard about this, he sent a letter to the [[Najashi|نَجَاشِي]] of Abyssinia, the king of what is now known as Ethiopia. And that was a Christian kingdom.
And what do you think the king of Abyssinia, who was a Christian, how do you think he felt when he knew that [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] killed 20,000 Christians? Of course, he became very angry.
So he sent an army from Abyssinia to [[Yemen|الْيَمَن]] to take control from [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]].
So the [[Najashi|نَجَاشِي]] of Abyssinia, he sent an army to [[Yemen|الْيَمَن]], and the leaders of this army were [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] and [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]].

[[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] and [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]. And you know [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], you have heard the name of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], because [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] later on, he would go to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and try to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]].

So this army from Abyssinia was sent to [[Yemen|الْيَمَن]], and they were able to take control from [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]]. And [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] tried to flee, he tried to escape. But while he was trying to escape, he drowned and he died in that way.

And Abyssinia took control of [[Yemen|الْيَمَن]]. If you remember from the first or second lesson, we said that [[Rabiah ibn Nasr|رَبِيعَة بن نَصْر]], he had a dream, he had a dream that the Abyssinians would take control of [[Yemen|الْيَمَن]]. Do you remember that? That the Abyssinians would take control of [[Yemen|الْيَمَن]].
And this is what happened. This is how the Abyssinians took control of [[Yemen|الْيَمَن]]. They came to take revenge for...

what was done to those Christians, and they exiled [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]]. They wanted to catch him, he tried to escape, but he was killed, he died while he was trying to flee. And the Abyssinian Christian kingdom took control of [[Yemen|اليمن]]
under the army of [[Abrahah|أبرهة]]. And they remained in control of [[Yemen|اليمن]] for about 70 years.
And you know the name of [[Abrahah|أبرهة]] because he is the one who then went on to try to destroy the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
And that incident happened in the year that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born, and that story is recounted in Surah al-Fil.
And that happened in the year of the birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, which we will get into next week [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]].

segments.translit: Wallāhu aʿlam, wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammad wa ʿalā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn.

segments.text: And Allah knows best, and may the peace, blessings, and grace of Allah be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions.

review.q: Who was the monk from [[Sham|شام]] whose miracles led the people of [[Najran|نجران]] to accept the true religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]]?
review.a: [[Faymiyun|فَيْمِيُون]] was a pious monk who prayed for a miracle that destroyed a worshipped tree, causing the city to convert to Christianity.

review.q: Why did the young [[Ghulam|غُلَام]] begin meeting the Christian monk in secret?
review.a: He encountered the monk while traveling to learn magic for King [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] and became mesmerized by the monk's recitation of the [[Injil|إنجيل]].

review.q: How did the boy seek a sign from Allah to determine whether the monk or the magician followed the truth?
review.a: He used a stone to kill a terrifying beast blocking the road, praying for its death if the monk's path was more beloved to Allah.

review.q: What names of Allah were demonstrated when the king's men failed to execute the boy by mountain or sea?
review.a: These events emphasized that Allah is [[al-Muhyi|المحيي]] (The Giver of Life) [[wa al-Mumit|والمميت]] (and the Giver of Death).

review.q: What specific phrase did King [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] have to say to successfully execute the boy?
review.a: The king was required to say, "[[Bismillahi Rabbil-Ghulam|بِسْمِ اللهِ رَبِّ الْغُلَامِ]]" (In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy) before shooting his arrow.

review.q: What was the result of the boy's public sacrifice during his execution?
review.a: The entire city realized the king's lack of power and declared their [[iman|إيمان]] in the Lord of the boy.

review.q: What miracle occurred during the massacre of the 20,000 believers to provide support to a hesitant mother?
review.a: A nursing baby spoke by Allah's permission to encourage his mother to stay firm on the truth as they faced the fire.

review.q: Who was the sole survivor of the trench massacre who escaped to seek help from the [[Najashi|نَجَاشِي]]?
review.a: [[Daws Dhu Tha'laban|دَوْس ذُو ثَعْلَبَان]] escaped on horseback and eventually informed the Abyssinian king, leading to the conquest of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
